subject: Packaging architecture — slab shift, feature carriage, and rollback options
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@healthatlas.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging architecture — slab shift, feature carriage, and rollback options

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a short note outlining how we think about the two packaging patterns you mentioned and to ask a few clarifying questions so we can surface a clean proposal. I attached our pricing matrix and a working slab proposal for reference.

High-level options we discussed:
- Consolidated slab (single committed throughput tier + included feature set) — predictable cost, simpler procurement.
- Modular add-ons (base tier + optional feature cartridges like private VPC, streaming, long-context KV cache) — more flexible, potentially lower starting commit.

Quick questions so we can model both paths accurately:
1) Expected steady-state monthly token throughput (approx tokens/month) and peak burst factor?
2) Which capabilities are must-have for launch (pick up to 3): streaming responses, private VPC, function/tool calling, long-context support, advanced tracing.
3) Any internal procurement constraints (e.g., minimum contract length, required discount thresholds, PO timing)?
4) Desired latency SLO for the most critical routes (p50/p95).

If you prefer, we can build a 90-day pilot offer for the slab vs. modular path side-by-side with modeled unit economics and a recommended rollback/upgrade clause.

Proposed next step: a short 30-minute packaging workshop with your engineering + procurement to align on numbers. Available times: Thu 10–12 or Fri 09–11 PT.

Attachments: 20260722-olga-slab-proposal.xlsx, redwood-pricing-matrix.pdf

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@healthatlas.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging architecture — slab shift, feature carriage, and rollback options

Hi Olga,

Appreciate the follow-up and the materials. Quick answers below to help you model:
- Throughput: currently ~120M tokens/month on our staging workloads, expecting 2x on production in Q4; planning for 3x burst for peak events.
- Must-have capabilities for launch: private VPC, streaming responses, and long-context support.
- Procurement: our standard is 12 months but we can do a 3-month pilot for proof. Procurement typically asks for a pilot discount >=10% and approval for any amendments takes about 10 business days.
- Latency SLO: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 500ms for routing-critical endpoints.

We are leaning toward a consolidated slab if the pilot terms include burst and a clear upgrade path without long lead procurement. Can you include a clause that allows a one-time mid-contract upgrade with prorated billing and automatic capacity burst for two scheduled events?

Also please include an option where we keep model artifacts in our VPC (private deployment) and Redwood provides the control plane only — list any differences in pricing for that setup.

Would like the packaging workshop tomorrow at 10:30 PT if that works — I’ll invite engineering and procurement.

Best,
Sarah Park
Head of Platform, HealthAtlas
sarah.park@healthatlas.com

Subject: Fwd: Packaging architecture — slab shift, feature carriage, and rollback options

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Sarah’s note (quoted below). Proposed workshop tomorrow 10:30 PT — Sarah will have procurement + infra. Need quick alignment on two draft offers so we can walk HealthAtlas through numbers:

Option 1 — Consolidated Slab (recommended)
- 12-month committed throughput slab but with a 90-day pilot at 20% pilot discount (to win the pilot).
- Includes private VPC add-on and streaming as part of the slab for pilot customers (to reduce frictions).
- Burst cover: 3x for two scheduled events per year; additional burst billed at standard overage rates.
- Mid-contract upgrade: allowed once, prorated billing, immediate capacity uplift.

Option 2 — Modular Add-ons
- 3-month pilot on a low commit base + modular feature cartridges (private VPC, streaming, long-context) at 10% pilot discount.
- Simpler step-up path but higher unit price after pilot compared to slab.

Questions for you:
- Ben: do we have authority to approve 20% pilot discount for strategic pilots? If not, what threshold?
- Karthik: rough estimate on whether private VPC with control plane-only billing should be treated as an addon (lower infra charge) or a separate SKU — I can walk through usage numbers in the workshop.

Olga

Subject: Re: Packaging architecture — slab shift, feature carriage, and rollback options

Hi all — thanks for the context and the pilot ask. I like the consolidated slab for HealthAtlas given expected scale and private deployment needs. Quick decisions/offer we can take into the workshop: 

Finalized pilot offer (to present tomorrow):
- Option A (Consolidated Slab, recommended): 90-day pilot with 20% pilot discount, committed slab sized at 150M tokens/month (accounts for near-term growth), includes private VPC and streaming features during pilot. Burst: 3x for two scheduled events in the pilot window; overage at published rates. Mid-contract upgrade allowed once, prorated.
- Option B (Modular Add-ons): 90-day pilot with 10% pilot discount; base commit 60M tokens/month + add-ons for private VPC and long-context; more expensive per-token but lower upfront commit.

Commercial notes and approvals:
- I can approve up to 15% standard pilot discount. 20% requires Sales Leader approval; I will escalate if we need 20% to secure pilot.
- For private deployment control-plane-only pricing, treat it as an addon SKU with a small infra surcharge (we will surface a separate line for infra + control plane in the quote). Karthik, can you confirm an estimate for the surcharge so we can show total TCO?

Next steps:
1) Olga to run the workshop tomorrow 10:30 PT.
2) After alignment, I’ll request Sales Leader approval for a 20% pilot discount (if HealthAtlas presses).
3) If HealthAtlas confirms Option A, legal will prepare a 90-day pilot SOW with a one-time upgrade clause and DocuSign link.

Attachment: 20260722-olga-slab-proposal.xlsx
DocuSign (draft SOW): https://app.docusign.com/samples/HLT-7891-pilot

Ben Carter
